 Kazakhstan to raise minimum wage
 12:46, 28 October 2026
 Kazakhstan plans to raise its minimum wage from 85,000 to 110,000 tenge on January 1, 2027. President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev instructed the government to implement the increase during his State-of-the-Nation Address, Qazinform News Agency reports.
 Photo credit: AI-generated / Qazinform 
 The increase will affect 1.8 million people, including over 370,000 workers paid from the state budget.
 “I instruct the government to raise the minimum wage from 85,000 to 110,000 tenge. This measure must take effect on January 1 next year,” Tokayev said. 
 Earlier, Qazinform News Agency reported that President Tokayev had proposed a three-year moratorium on inspections of micro- and small businesses from January 1, 2027.
